name: Germany
tagline: Sixteen states that were separate countries within living memory, and still behave like it.
summary: Germany has no single centre because it was assembled from kingdoms and free cities in 1871, and every one of them kept its own capital, cathedral and beer. That is the country's real pleasure: Bavaria and Hamburg have less in common than France and Spain. Berlin is a city of the twentieth century, still visibly working through it; the Rhine, the Black Forest and the Baltic coast are all quieter than they deserve.

season.note: May and September are the best of it. December is Christmas market season and genuinely worth the cold — the markets are civic events, not tourist ones. Oktoberfest is in September, which catches people out annually.

getting_around: ICE trains link the big cities fast, and the Deutschlandticket gives a month of unlimited regional transport nationwide for a flat fee — the best transport deal in Europe. Regional trains reach almost every valley.
food: Bread: 3,000 registered varieties, and the bakery is the first thing to find
Wurst, which is regional and non-negotiable — Currywurst in Berlin, Weisswurst before noon only in Munich
Riesling from the Mosel, which is dry now whatever your grandmother thought

festivals.name: Christmas markets
festivals.where: Nuremberg, Dresden, and every town square

know: Cash is still king in a surprising number of bakeries, bars and taxis.
Sunday closing is near-total; buy food on Saturday.
Jaywalking against a red man is genuinely disapproved of, especially with children present.

regions.name: Berlin & the East
regions.summary: The capital, Saxony's baroque cities, and the landscape of a country that was two countries.

cities.name: Berlin
cities.summary: Poor, sexy, enormous and unfinished — five museums on one island and a wall memorial that refuses to be comfortable.
highlights: Museum Island, especially the Pergamon's scale and the Neues Museum's Nefertiti
The Berlin Wall Memorial at Bernauer Straße — the honest one, not Checkpoint Charlie
Tempelhof: an airport turned into the largest urban park in the world
The Stasi Museum, in the ministry's own offices

experiences.name: The Wall, where it stood
experiences.summary: Bernauer Straße preserves the death strip, the tunnels and the names — an hour that does what no film manages.

experiences.name: Cycle the runways at Tempelhof
experiences.summary: Two 2,000-metre runways, open to anyone, kept deliberately empty by referendum.

cities.name: Dresden
cities.summary: A baroque royal capital burned in 1945 and rebuilt stone by numbered stone, on a river bend.
highlights: The Frauenkirche, reassembled from the rubble and finished in 2005
The Green Vault's treasury, booked in timed slots
Saxon Switzerland's sandstone towers, forty minutes upriver

cities.name: Leipzig
cities.summary: Bach's church, a peaceful revolution that started in it, and a cotton mill full of painters.
highlights: Bach's Thomaskirche, where he was cantor for 27 years
The Nikolaikirche and the Monday demonstrations of 1989
Spinnerei: a vast mill turned gallery quarter

regions.name: Bavaria & the Alps
regions.summary: Beer halls, baroque churches, mountain lakes and a mad king's castles.

cities.name: Munich
cities.summary: A wealthy southern capital with the Alps an hour away and a river you can surf in the middle of a park.
highlights: The Eisbach standing wave, surfed year-round in the English Garden
The Alte Pinakothek's Rubens and Dürer
A beer garden where you may legally bring your own food
Day trains to the mountains and the lakes

experiences.name: A beer garden, done correctly
experiences.summary: Buy the beer, bring the food, sit at the unmarked communal tables — the marked ones are for served customers and the distinction matters.

cities.name: Berchtesgaden
cities.summary: An alpine corner surrounded on three sides by Austria, with a fjord-green lake below the Watzmann.
highlights: Königssee, crossed by electric boats since 1909 so the echo carries
The salt mine, worked since 1517, entered on a wooden slide
Steep, serious walking on the Watzmann

experiences.name: The trumpet on the Königssee
experiences.summary: The boatman stops mid-lake and plays into the cliff; the echo comes back a full phrase later.

regions.name: The Rhine & the West
regions.summary: Castles on a gorge, Riesling on impossible slopes, and cathedral cities strung along the river.

cities.name: Cologne
cities.summary: A Roman city with a Gothic cathedral that took 632 years and dominates everything.
highlights: The Dom, and 533 steps up the south tower
Kölsch served in 200 ml glasses, replaced until you cover it with the mat
The Roman-Germanic museum's mosaic, found while digging an air-raid shelter

cities.name: Bacharach & the Rhine Gorge
cities.summary: Half-timbered wine village under a ruined chapel, in the 65-kilometre UNESCO stretch of castles.
highlights: Forty castles in sixty-five kilometres of river
Riesling from slate slopes at 60 degrees
The Rheinsteig path along the eastern rim

experiences.name: Above the vineyards on the Rheinsteig
experiences.summary: The high path gives you the whole gorge; the trains and boats below give you the way back.

regions.name: The North
regions.summary: Hanseatic brick, harbour cities and a Baltic coast of white cliffs and beach chairs.

cities.name: Hamburg
cities.summary: A merchant republic and Europe's third port, with more bridges than Venice and Amsterdam together.
highlights: The Elbphilharmonie, and its free public plaza at 37 metres
Speicherstadt's brick warehouse city on oak piles
Fischmarkt at 5 am on a Sunday, with a band

experiences.name: The 62 ferry, not the tour boat
experiences.summary: A public transport ferry down the Elbe past the container terminals; same view, a fraction of the price.

cities.name: Lübeck
cities.summary: The queen of the Hanseatic League, on an island, in brick gothic, and the home of marzipan.
highlights: The Holstentor, leaning and famous and on the old fifty-mark note
Seven towers on the island skyline
Thomas Mann's family house, and Buddenbrooks written in it
